## Natural history notes

A wood-decay crust fungus characterized by hard, flat to slightly raised brownish patches that grow tightly against bark or exposed wood rather than forming a typical cap or bracket. In Florida, it is found on dead or declining hardwood trees, branches, logs, and wounds in hammocks, forests, parks, yards, and other wooded habitats. It acts as a decomposer and sometimes a heart-rot fungus, breaking down woody tissue and recycling nutrients while producing spores from tiny pore-like openings across the crust surface.
